clue.text: Unorthodox vicar with ring: 1 in 7 or possible 10 of 22 across

indicators.note: something unorthodox departs from the usual order, so the letters of vicar are rearranged

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

indicators.note: the word in tells us the figure 1 goes inside the spelt-out 7

parts.note: the number seven written out in letters
the figure one looks like the letter I (a Roman numeral)

explanation.surface: A nonconformist clergyman with a ring, plus a puzzling sum, linked to a sign of getting old.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers are not cross-references to other lights: '1 in 7' means the figure inside the spelt-out number. Only '10 of 22 across' points to other answers, a sign of ageing.
explanation.definitionFit: Swollen, twisted leg vessels commonly appear with advancing years, so they are a possible symptom of growing old.

clue.text: See 1
Curve left, away from climb

indicators.note: away from says the letter for left is taken out of the word for climb

parts.note: to clamber is to climb awkwardly

explanation.surface: A bend in the road leaves you no longer climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A road's slight arch or convex curve across its surface is its camber.

clue.text: Ring relatives on a west American Pacific island

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
kin are one's relatives
W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Phoning family on a US-held island in the western Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Okinawa is a Japanese island in the Pacific, long home to American military bases.

clue.text: What pioneers do: invade, settle and educate leaders

parts.note: the punctuation mark printed in the clue is itself a colon

indicators.note: leaders are the front runners, here the opening letters of the three verbs

explanation.surface: A list of the things frontier settlers did: invaded, stayed put and taught.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation mark after 'do' looks like mere grammar, but it is part of the wordplay and names itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Pioneers settle new territory and establish communities there, which is exactly to found colonies.

clue.text: The Titanic's claim to be lacking power outside Belfast, for example

indicators.note: outside says the phrase for lacking power wraps around the kitchen fitting

parts.note: to be unable is to lack the power to do something
a Belfast sink is a deep ceramic kitchen sink, so Belfast is an example of a sink

explanation.surface: The famous ship, built in Belfast, was said to be beyond sinking yet was powerless.
explanation.walkthrough: A Belfast sink is a large square white ceramic sink common in British kitchens; the Titanic was also built in Belfast, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The liner was famously advertised as a ship that could never go down, a boast proved disastrously false.

clue.text: Egoist rolling a cigar

indicators.note: rolling suggests turning over and over, so the letters of Egoist are shuffled

explanation.surface: A self-obsessed man rolling himself a cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A stogie is a long, cheap, slender cigar, the name coming from Conestoga in Pennsylvania.

clue.text: Attempt to counter 10s of 22 across on front cover

parts.note: the face is the front of something, as in a building's face
a mask is a cover for the face

explanation.surface: A beauty treatment for the front of the head meant to fight the years.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty mask applied to the skin is a cosmetic attempt to reduce wrinkles and other marks of age.

clue.text: Trains are not busy

indicators.note: trains in the sense of shapes or drills into a new form, so are not is rearranged

explanation.surface: Railway services are quiet today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' looks like the subject of a sentence about railways, but it is the anagram signal working on 'are not'.
explanation.definitionFit: An over-decorated design is called busy, meaning elaborately and fussily ornamented.

clue.text: Initial clue

definitions.meaning: to initial a document is to put your mark of approval on it
a clue is an indication or hint of something

explanation.definitionFit: To initial a document is to autograph it with letters, and a hint or indication is also this word.

clue.text: House flies on sagging flesh (hers)

parts.note: house is the call in bingo, and a name for the game itself
wings are what a creature flies on

explanation.surface: A housefly landing on a woman's flabby skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is the call made on a full card in bingo, the British hall game. BINGO WINGS is British slang for loose flesh hanging from the upper arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang term names the loose flesh on the back of the upper arm, said to wobble when bingo players wave.

clue.text: An apartment right for a high flier?

parts.note: a condo is an apartment in a condominium block

explanation.surface: A flat fit for someone who lives high up?
explanation.definitionFit: The Andean condor is a vulture that soars at great altitude, so it is literally a high-flying bird.

clue.text: Dublin Echo spread: "Sagging flesh (his 'n' hers)"

indicators.note: spread suggests letters laid out loosely, so Dublin Echo is rearranged

explanation.surface: An Irish newspaper's spread is headlined about saggy flesh in men and women.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dublin Echo looks like an Irish newspaper and 'spread' like a newspaper feature, but 'spread' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold of fat beneath the jaw affects both sexes, unlike the arm flab of the other clue.

clue.text: With sheet of ice, boy creates a 10 of 22 across

definitions.note: the definition is singular, but the answer is plural: lines on the skin collectively count as one sign

parts.note: a rink is a sheet of ice for skating
Les is a boy's name, short for Leslie

explanation.surface: A lad on an ice rink produces signs of age.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines and creases in the skin are a classic indication that a person is getting older.

clue.text: Plant's rendition of Blue Monday?

definitions.note: read as plant is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: a rendition is a fresh performance or version, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's version of the famous pop song about a gloomy start to the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue Monday' looks like the song title, but it supplies BLUE plus MON, the abbreviation for Monday, as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelumbo is the botanical genus of lotus plants, aquatic flowering species with large round leaves.

clue.text: 10 of 22 across? Stalin out East after party uprising

indicators.note: after places the tyrant without the letter behind the reversed party
uprising in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the British Labour Party

indicators.note: out says the compass letter is removed from the tyrant

parts.note: Stalin is a classic example of a despot
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Stalin was ousted in the East after a party revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns LAB into BAL; 'out' removes E from DESPOT, leaving DSPOT. Stalin defines DESPOT by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch of hairless scalp is a familiar mark of a man getting older.

clue.text: Fish bearing down with French head of state

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a compass bearing
a bas is the French for down with, as in a slogan

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of state is taken

explanation.surface: Bearing down on the French president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down with French' is a phrase to translate: the slogan 'à bas', meaning down with, gives ABAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea bass is a type of marine fish prized for eating.

clue.text: Players act out of strange fascination

indicators.note: out of says the letters of act are taken away from the larger word
strange suggests something odd or jumbled, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Actors perform out of a weird obsession.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A, C and T from FASCINATION, and 'strange' rearranges the remaining FSINIONA.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinfonia is a small orchestra, so it is a group of musical players.

clue.text: Hosts miss lapping up milk products

indicators.note: lapping means going round, so the title for a woman wraps the reversed milk word

parts.note: Ms is a title for a woman, like miss

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: dairy is the collective term for milk products

explanation.surface: Party hosts miss out on drinking the milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DAIRY into YRIAD, which MS surrounds. 'Lapping' looks like a cat drinking milk.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great multitude, so hosts and vast numbers mean the same.

clue.text: Throw money at pine tree

parts.note: to lob is to throw something in a high arc
lolly is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Throwing cash at a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: LOLLY is everyday British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The loblolly is a species of pine native to the south-eastern United States.

clue.text: Making public sally

definitions.meaning: revealing something, especially a person's sexuality, to everyone
a sally is a jaunt or excursion

explanation.definitionFit: Exposing someone's private life is called this, and a short trip or excursion is also this word.

clue.text: Lord unseated from a horse, when getting on

indicators.note: unseated from says the abbreviation for lord is thrown off the horse

parts.note: a gelding is a castrated male horse

explanation.surface: A nobleman falls off a horse in his old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unseated from' removes L and D, scattered, from GELDING to leave GEING.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing old.

clue.text: A fine fabric — it's glowing

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
lame is a fabric woven with metallic threads

explanation.surface: A fine, shimmering cloth is glowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ablaze is burning and shining brightly.

clue.text: Supplies drawer for stationery, say

definitions.note: the word for writing paper sounds like a word meaning motionless

parts.note: stocks are supplies kept in reserve
a till is a cash drawer in a shop

explanation.surface: Office supplies kept in a drawer for paper and pens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stationery, say' means a word sounding like stationery, so read it as stationary.
explanation.definitionFit: Being motionless is to be completely without movement.

clue.text: Low noise? I try to cover Duke's classic number

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
din is a loud noise
D is the abbreviation for duke
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: A singer covering a famous Duke Ellington tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' is surface dressing for a cover version; Duke Ellington's famous jazz piece is the answer. 'Low' is the noise cattle make.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke Ellington's 1930 jazz standard is one of the best-known classic tunes of the era.

clue.text: Setter's 2, perhaps

definitions.meaning: belonging to me, the setter writing the puzzle
clue 2, a seam of ore in rock, can loosely stand for a pit dug to extract it

explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun means belonging to me, and a pit worked for ore also shares the word.

clue.text: See 24
10 of 22 across when half-dead soldiers return key

indicators.note: half signals taking only the first two letters of dead

parts.note: men are soldiers, as in officers and men

indicators.note: return means the word for key is read backwards

parts.note: a key is a low island, as is an ait

explanation.surface: Ageing troops come back home when half dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns AIT (a small river island) into TIA. 'key' looks like a lock's key but is an island, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory and mental decline is a common condition of old age.
